description: “We are a team of six passionate students ready to explore space, solve problems, and think beyond boundaries. Together, we aim to learn, innovate, and create something meaningful through NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026!” 🚀
summary:
The Ones We Left Behind is an educational storytelling project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten."

The project explores the stories of 13 groups of NASA spacecraft and robotic equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Through illustrated first-person narratives, readers discover the missions, scientific contributions, discoveries, and final status of these space explorers.

The project combines creative storytelling with scientific information through mission data cards, visual illustrations, and educational activities. It also includes NASA mission references to help readers explore and verify the information.

Designed for young space enthusiasts aged 8–14, the project aims to make space exploration history engaging, accessible, and educational.

Team: Interstellar_0001
details: > The Ones We Left Behind is an illustrated storybook for ages 8–14 about 13 groups of NASA machines left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space: Surveyor, Apollo Eagle's descent stage, the Moon buggies, ALSEP, Viking, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Phoenix and InSight, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and 11, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn and Kepler. Each machine tells its own last chapter in first person, and every page has a Mission Data Card with real facts (dates, distances, counts, outcomes) from the NASA mission pages in the challenge Resources list. Readers learn what each machine was built to do, what it discovered, and where it rests now. The book ends with three hands-on activities. Benefit: it turns dense mission history into something a child can read and enjoy, and it links engineering to the science it made possible. Tools: Python and the ReportLab library to build the PDF layout and vector art, and Claude (Anthropic) to draft text and generate the illustrations. The story is creative because the robots narrate their own endings. The team considered age-appropriate language, accessibility (large high-contrast text, a printable PDF), accuracy, and clear AI labeling.
